extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) working on office actions
extracted.subtask_description: Selection and use of consolidated MPEP §700 form paragraphs for Office actions, including standards for explaining rejections, finality, responses to applicant arguments, and rules for continued examination and transitional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim noncompliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(d)/pre-AIA 112, fourth paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim does not comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(d) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, fourth paragraph, the dependent claim should be rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112(d) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, fourth paragraph, as unpatentable rather than objecting to the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant case law (e.g., 79 USPQ2d 1583, 1589-90 (Fed. Cir. 2006)). See also MPEP §608.01(n), subsection III, 'Infringement Test' for dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37 Arguments Are Not Persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments filed [1] have been fully considered but they are not persuasive. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must address all arguments not already responded to in the statement of rejection (bracket 1: identify applicant remarks; bracket 2: explanation of non-persuasiveness). This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.02 Unpersuasive Argument: Bodily Incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: The test for obviousness is not whether features of a secondary reference may be bodily incorporated into the primary reference; the test is what the combined teachings of the references would have suggested to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In responding to applicant’s argument that [1], briefly restate applicant’s arguments (bracket 1). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re Keller, 642 F.2d 413, 208 USPQ 871 (CCPA 1981).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.03 Unpersuasive Argument: Hindsight Reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Any judgment on obviousness is necessarily a reconstruction based on hindsight reasoning, but it is proper if it accounts only for knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time and does not include knowledge gleaned only from the applicant’s disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re McLaughlin, 443 F.2d 1392, 170 USPQ 209 (CCPA 1971).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.01 Unpersuasive Argument: Age of Reference(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to applicant’s argument that there is no teaching, suggestion, or motivation to combine the references, obviousness may be established by combining or modifying teachings where some teaching, suggestion, or motivation is found either in the references or in knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain where the TSM (teaching/suggestion/motivation) for the rejection is found (either in the references or in general knowledge) in bracket 1. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re Fine, In re Jones, and KSR v. Teleflex.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.04 Unpersuasive Argument: No Teaching, Suggestion, or Motivation To Combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Response template for applicant’s contention that there is no teaching, suggestion, or motivation to combine references; applicant’s arguments have been considered but are not persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must explain non-persuasiveness in bracket 2 and address all unresponded arguments. This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.05 Unpersuasive Argument: Nonanalogous Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art reference must either be in the field of the applicant’s endeavor or be reasonably pertinent to the particular problem with which the applicant was concerned to be relied upon for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, enter the name of the reference applicant alleges is nonanalogous; in bracket 2 explain why the reference is analogous art. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re Oetiker, 977 F.2d 1443, 24 USPQ2d 1443 (Fed. Cir. 1992).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.06 Unpersuasive Argument: Number of References
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on a large number of references in a rejection does not, without more, weigh against the obviousness of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph where applicant argues too many references were combined. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re Gorman, 933 F.2d 982, 18 USPQ2d 1885 (Fed. Cir. 1991).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.07 Unpersuasive Argument: Applicant Obtains Result Not Contemplated by Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of another advantage flowing naturally from following the suggestion of the prior art cannot be the basis for patentability when the differences would otherwise be obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly restate applicant’s arguments re: results not contemplated in bracket 1. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite Ex parte Obiaya, 227 USPQ 58 (Bd. Pat. App. & Inter. 1985).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.08 Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Limitations Which Are Not Claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant relies on features not recited in the rejected claim(s), those features should not be read into the claims; claims are interpreted in light of the specification but limitations from the specification are not read into the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, recite the features applicant relies upon but which are not recited in the claims. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.09 Unpersuasive Argument: Intended Use
rubrics_metrics.description: A recitation of the intended use of the claimed invention must result in a structural difference between the claimed invention and the prior art to patentably distinguish; if the prior art structure can perform the intended use, it meets the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly restate applicant’s arguments about intended use in bracket 1. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.10 Unpersuasive Argument: Limitation(s) in Preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble is generally not accorded patentable weight where it merely recites the purpose of a process or intended use of a structure and the body of the claim stands alone; recitations in the preamble will not be given patentable weight absent structural dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1, state the preamble recitation applicant is arguing about. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re Hirao and Kropa v. Robie.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.11 Unpersuasive Argument: General Allegation of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments that amount to general allegations that the claims define a patentable invention fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b) because they do not specifically point out how claim language patentably distinguishes from references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when applicant's response is a general assertion of patentability without specific comparison to cited art. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.12 Unpersuasive Argument: Novelty Not Clearly Pointed Out
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph heading present (text not fully included in this chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content for this paragraph not present in the supplied chunk; when used, it addresses failure to clearly point out novelty in applicant’s arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.37.13 Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Against References Individually
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually where the rejection is based on combinations of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Cite In re Keller and In re Merck & Co.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.38 Arguments Are Moot Because of New Ground(s) of Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments with respect to claim [1] have been considered but are moot because the arguments do not apply to any of the references being used in the current rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must still address any applicant arguments that remain relevant to any references being applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.38.01 Arguments Persuasive, Previous Rejection/Objection Withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments, see [1], filed [2], with respect to [3] have been fully considered and are persuasive. The [4] of [5] has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracket instructions: identify pages/lines of applicant remarks (bracket1), file date (bracket2), claims/figures/specification (bracket3), the rejection/objection being withdrawn (bracket4), and the new ground(s) or subject matter (bracket5). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.38.02 Arguments Persuasive, New Ground(s) of Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments do not comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c) because they do not clearly point out the patentable novelty which they think the claims present in view of the art or show how amendments avoid such references or objections. Applicant’s arguments, filed [2], are persuasive; the rejection has been withdrawn but a new ground(s) of rejection is made in view of [5].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must identify applicant arguments (bracket1), filing date (bracket2), claims at issue (bracket3), statutory basis for previous rejection (bracket4), and the basis for the new ground(s) of rejection (bracket5). Precede with form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.39 Action Is Final
rubrics_metrics.description: THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a). A shortened statutory period for reply to this final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date; if a first reply is filed within TWO MONTHS and the advisory action is mailed after the THREE-MONTH period, then the shortened period expires on the advisory action mailing date; statutory period never later than SIX MONTHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use in reissue litigation cases or reexamination proceedings (special SSPs). Guidance includes calculation of extension fees under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and exceptions for reissue/reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.39.01 Final Rejection, Options for Applicant, Pro Se
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is a final rejection intended to close prosecution. Applicant’s reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is limited to either an appeal to the PTAB or an amendment complying with stated requirements. Notice of Appeal must be filed within the reply period and accompanied by appeal fee $[1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-final amendments that touch the merits are not a matter of right unless they merely cancel claims or comply with earlier formal requirements; they may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons for not presenting them earlier. A reply must include the appeal from or cancellation of each rejected claim. This form paragraph must be preceded by any one of listed form paragraphs (7.39, 7.40, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.40 Action Is Final, Necessitated by Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Applicant is reminded of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy and the shortened reply periods described in ¶7.39.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §706.07(a). This form paragraph should not be used in reissue litigation or reexamination proceedings as noted for SSP calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.40.01 Action Is Final, Necessitated by IDS With Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s submission of an information disclosure statement under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) on [1] prompted the new ground(s) of rejection presented. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Applicant is reminded of extension policy under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with MPEP §609.04(b). Insert filing date of IDS in bracket 1. Do not use where other new grounds were introduced not necessitated by IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.40.02.aia Action Is Final, Necessitated by Invoking the Joint Research Agreement Prior Art Exclusion Under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s submission of requirements for the JRA prior art exclusion under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) on [1] prompted the new double patenting rejection presented. THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Applicant is reminded of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 where claims are examined under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102/103. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. Insert filing date of submission for JRA exclusion in bracket 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.40.02.fti Action Is Final, Necessitated by Invoking the Joint Research Agreement Prior Art Exclusion Under Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s submission of requirements for the JRA prior art exclusion under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) on [1] prompted the new double patenting rejection presented. THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Applicant is reminded of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert filing date of submission for the JRA exclusion under pre-AIA 103(c) in bracket 1. Do not use where other new grounds were introduced not necessitated by amendments/IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.41 Action Is Final, First Action
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a [1] of applicant’s earlier Application No. [2]. All claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered earlier. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action in this case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert '--continuation--' or '--substitute--' in bracket 1. See MPEP §706.07(b). Do not use if amendment was refused entry in parent case for raising new issues or new matter. SSP and 37 CFR 1.136(a) exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.41.01.fti Transitional After Final Practice, First Submission (37 CFR 1.129(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under transitional practice, if application pending at least two years as of June 8, 1995, applicant is entitled to have a first submission entered/considered on the merits if filed prior to abandonment with fee 37 CFR 1.17(r). Payment may withdraw finality of prior action; amendments cannot introduce new matter under 35 U.S.C. 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert fee amount for entity and identify entity size (brackets). If multiple conflicting proposed amendments exist, provide instructions upon payment. May follow form paragraphs 7.39-7.41 in applicable pre-June 9, 1995 cases. Not for design or reissue or reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.41.02.fti Transitional After Final Practice, Second Submission (37 CFR 1.129(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a first submission fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r) was previously paid, applicant is entitled to have a second submission entered and considered on the merits upon timely filing and payment of fee 1.17(r); finality of previous Office action will be withdrawn. No amendment introducing new matter per 35 U.S.C. 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert fee amount and entity status in brackets. Use for applications filed prior to June 9, 1995 where first submission fee already paid. Follow form paragraphs 7.39-7.41 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.41.03 Action Is Final, First Action Following Submission Under 37 CFR 1.53(d), CPA in a Design Application
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the parent application prior to filing of the CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds/art of record in the next Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action after filing under 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remind applicant of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy and shortened reply periods. This is for design CPAs under 1.53(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42 Withdrawal of Finality of Last Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s request for reconsideration of the finality of the rejection of the last Office action is persuasive and the finality of that action is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where reconsideration is persuasive and explain basis for withdrawal. Bracket insertions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.01.fti Withdrawal of Finality of Last Office Action - Transitional Application Under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since application is eligible for transitional 1.129(a) and fee 1.17(r) has been timely paid, the finality of the previous Office action has been withdrawn pursuant to 37 CFR 1.129(a). Applicant’s [1] submission after final filed on [2] has been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert '--first--' or '--second--' in bracket 1 and date(s) in bracket 2. Not for design or reissue or reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.02.fti Nonresponsive Submission Filed Under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The timely submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed on [1] is not fully responsive to the prior Office action because [2]. Since the submission appears bona fide, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO MONTHS from the mailing date to submit a complete reply; this supersedes the previous time period and may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If an appeal was previously filed, payment of 1.17(r) is construed as request to dismiss appeal and continue prosecution under 1.129(a); the appeal stands dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must set forth reasons why the submission is not fully responsive in bracket 2 and insert date of receipt in bracket 1. Use when submission is bona fide but nonresponsive; follow rules for dismissal of appeals and calculation of deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.03.fti Action Is Final, First Action Following Submission Under 37 CFR 1.129(a) Filed Prior to June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions under 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005, if all claims are drawn to same invention claimed prior to entry under 1.129(a) and could have been finally rejected earlier, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is first action after the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §706.07(b). Remind applicant of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy; use 7.41.02.fti when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.031.fti Action Is Final, Action Following Submission Under 37 CFR 1.129(a) Filed On or After June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: Under final action practice for Office actions following a 1.129(a) submission filed on/after June 8, 2005, the next Office action will be equivalent to the next action following a reply to a non-final action and will be made final except where examiner introduces a new ground of rejection not necessitated by applicant’s amendment nor based on IDS information filed in the 1.97(c) period with fee 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no new ground is introduced beyond those necessitated by amendment/IDS, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL. Remind applicant of 37 CFR 1.136(a) extension policy. Also reference use of 7.41.02.fti if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.04 Continued Examination under 37 CFR 1.114 after Final Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 including fee 1.17(e) was filed after final rejection; since application is eligible and fee timely paid, the finality of the previous action is withdrawn and applicant’s submission filed on [1] has been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when RCE and submission were filed after final rejection. In bracket 1 insert date(s) of receipt. Submission may include IDS, amendments, new arguments, or new evidence. To be eligible, application must meet filing-type/date requirements; RCE must be filed on/after May 29, 2000. If submission does not comply with 1.111 use 7.42.08 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.05 Continued Examination Under 37 CFR 1.114 After Allowance or Quayle Action
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 including fee 1.17(e) was filed after allowance or after an Ex parte Quayle action; since eligible and fee paid, prosecution is reopened and the submission filed on [1] has been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use if RCE filed after notice of allowance or Quayle action. Insert date(s) of receipt in bracket 1. Application must meet eligibility requirements as for other RCEs; if RCE filed after issue fee paid, petition under 1.313 to withdraw from issue must have been filed and granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.42.06 Continued Examination Under 37 CFR 1.114 After Appeal But Before A Board Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 was filed after appeal to the PTAB but prior to a decision; since eligible and fee 1.17(e) timely paid, the appeal has been withdrawn and prosecution reopened; applicant’s submission filed on [1] has been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when RCE filed after Notice of Appeal or appeal brief but before Board decision; submission may include IDS, amendments, new arguments/evidence, or previously filed appeal briefs incorporated into the RCE. Insert date(s) in bracket 1.
